purpose: Independent classical-MD check (EAM) of the GB10's MACE melting point and latent heat.
status: inputs only; NOT submitted. Ask Madhan before submitting any Nebius job.
engine: LAMMPS (needs the MANYBODY package: check `lmp -h | grep -i eam` on the Nebius image)

potential.citation: Y. Mishin, M.J. Mehl, D.A. Papaconstantopoulos, A.F. Voter, and J.D. Kress (2001), "Structural stability and lattice defects in copper: Ab initio, tight-binding, and embedded-atom calculations", Physical Review B 63(22), 224106.
caveats: This is the paper's EAM1 potential (NIST notes: 'This listing is for the reference's EAM1 potential'); its EAM2 is listed without LAMMPS files.
NIST's own iprPy two-phase estimate for this implementation is 1323.26 +/- 1.46 K (fcc), on its implementation page. Context only; it does not set the bracket or the reference.
The abstract (as listed on NIST) does not name the melting point among the fitted or reproduced properties; the paper's fitting database itself was not checked.

fingerprint_check.source: release notes (SOLD vs LAMMPS minimum energy)

nist_computed_melting_K.method: NIST iprPy melting_temperature (two-phase, NPH + Berendsen, 200,000 steps)

structure.source: coolorbit/sim/alloys.py ELEMENT_CRYSTALS (Donohue, The Structures of the Elements, 1974; alpha-Ga: Sharma & Donohue 1962). Starting lattice constants; NPT relaxes them.

melting_point_guess.source: data/calibration/tier1.json (ITS-90 defining fixed point, NIST https://its90.nist.gov/TerminologyFPoint)
melting_point_guess.use: ONLY to place the temperature bracket. Not a reference value: the calibration references live in data/calibration/ (Teammate 1).

jobs.command: lmp -in ../in.coexist.lmp -log log_Cu-coexist-T1086.2.lammps -var T 1086.2 -var Tprep 1357.8 -var Tmelt 4073.4 -var seed 2026
lmp -in ../in.coexist.lmp -log log_Cu-coexist-T1222.lammps -var T 1222 -var Tprep 1357.8 -var Tmelt 4073.4 -var seed 2026
lmp -in ../in.coexist.lmp -log log_Cu-coexist-T1357.8.lammps -var T 1357.8 -var Tprep 1357.8 -var Tmelt 4073.4 -var seed 2026
lmp -in ../in.coexist.lmp -log log_Cu-coexist-T1493.5.lammps -var T 1493.5 -var Tprep 1357.8 -var Tmelt 4073.4 -var seed 2026
lmp -in ../in.coexist.lmp -log log_Cu-coexist-T1629.3.lammps -var T 1629.3 -var Tprep 1357.8 -var Tmelt 4073.4 -var seed 2026

jobs.command: lmp -in ../in.latent.lmp -log log_Cu-latent-solid.lammps -var phase solid -var T TM_MEAM_K -var seed 2026

jobs.status: BLOCKED until this potential's own melting point is known from the coexistence jobs (latent heat is defined at the model's Tm, not the experimental one)
jobs.command: lmp -in ../in.latent.lmp -log log_Cu-latent-liquid.lammps -var phase liquid -var T TM_MEAM_K -var seed 2026

latent.protocol: solid vs liquid enthalpy at Tm

analysis.latent: python ../analyze.py latent h_solid_TTM_MEAM_K.dat h_liquid_TTM_MEAM_K.dat --log-solid log_Cu-latent-solid.lammps --log-liquid log_Cu-latent-liquid.lammps

if_bracket_missed: all melting -> shift the bracket down by 20%; all freezing -> up by 20% (same rule as the GB10 Simulator), then refine around the crossover with 4 temperatures 2% apart.
